people.role: Founder (970) and head of Dạ Quang Môn; the desert raider who knelt to Băng Tâm in 1121
people.appearance: A huge grey-bearded rider with a burn across one side of his face and a jade cup that glows on his belt at night.
people.backstory: Hạng Dạ Bôi was born in 870 into the Hạng, a caravan-guard family of Trường Vân Thành (A120), and rode the Pavilion's caravan road for eighty years. In 968 a caravan of Băng Tâm's tax silver was lost to the sand, and the Desert Pavilion hanged his elder brother for it. Two years later Hạng took the guards the Pavilion had dismissed and became the thing they had guarded against: Dạ Quang Môn, bound to no lord (C172). For a century and a half his raiders drank grape wine from night-glowing cups after every raid and left one cup behind as their mark (A121). In 1119 Băng Tâm marched (C184). In 1121 it burned Huyết Đao Trại, where his loot was hidden and his first wife Lâu Minh Châu (lau_minh_chau) died (V074). He knelt to Sở Ngọc Hồ (so_ngoc_ho) and gave her his son Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa) as surety (C185). Since then his riders have guarded the caravans they used to rob (A123), and since 1194 the Pavilion's silver for loads delivered has come in heavier every year. He takes it and does not ask his wife where her band rides. He is 330, and he has not forgiven anything. When his young blades began drinking from the cups again (A126), he poured the first one himself.
people.wants: His son home before he dies, and one day to watch the Keeper of the Vessel kneel.
people.secret: The Pavilion burned the wrong fort. Dạ Quang's real hoard lies under the sand at Mai Sa Bảo, buried in 1050 (V073): enough stones to hire a war.

people.role: Hạng Dạ Bôi's second wife and first blade; runs the Đà Linh road as a toll, and her band strikes the trains that ride without Dạ Quang
people.appearance: A lean desert woman in red felt, with a hawk feather knotted to her sabre and a smile that the Pavilion's envoys do not like.
people.backstory: Đồ Xích Linh grew up in the felt tents of Chiên Trướng Thôn and rode with Dạ Quang from the age of sixteen. By 1100 she led its fastest band. In the Taming (C184) she killed more Băng Tâm riders than anyone, and took the sabre of one of them, a hawk feather still on its hilt. She did not kneel in 1121; she was not asked, because the Pavilion did not know her name. She married Hạng Dạ Bôi (hang_da_boi) four years later, after Lâu Minh Châu (lau_minh_chau) burned, and gave him a daughter, Hạng Lưu Hỏa (hang_luu_hoa). To her the knee was a pause, not an end. In 1194, when the young blades took up the cups again (A126), she found a better use for them than raiding: the Pavilion pays its escorts by loads delivered, so she made every load that did not hire Dạ Quang unsafe. Her band rides with wrapped faces and leaves no cup. She has never met her stepson Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa), and she means to keep it so. She buys a blood art layer by layer from the ma đạo cultivator Triệu Huyết Y (trieu_huyet_y) and pays in stones from her own gambling.
people.wants: The road kept as it is: Dạ Quang's tally the highest the Pavilion pays, and every small train on it paying her for the privilege of arriving. The hostage kept at the Pavilion, because a son raised beside the keeper of the caravan road would ride with Ô Liệt Phong and end it. After that, Dạ Quang unbound, within her husband's lifetime or after it.
people.secret: Her band strikes the trains that ride without Dạ Quang while Ô Liệt Phong is out on the long leg; she reads his legs off the board at the Đà Linh well, and buys Trấn Sa's routes from Tất Dạ Lang so that the band never meets a Trấn Sa guard (she does not know Viên Cô Yên makes them false). The drivers it takes are fed to Cừu Lạc Nhật's sabre with Triệu Huyết Y's art. And she has Cổ Xích Nguyệt leave a cup at a caravan stop each season, so that the Pavilion stays uneasy and keeps her stepson.

people.role: Hạng Dạ Bôi's daughter; leader of the young blades, who ride in her mother's band
people.appearance: Her father's height and her mother's smile, in a riding coat with a night-glow cup sewn on the breast.
people.backstory: Born after the knee, she never raided until her mother gave her a band. In 1194 she was the first to drink from the night-glowing cups again (A126), and half the young blades of Dạ Quang now follow her past Dương Bằng with wrapped faces. Her mother Đồ Xích Linh (do_xich_linh) gave her the road, and she likes what it pays. She has never met her half-brother Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa), and every year she writes to him that the road is quiet.
people.wants: To ride at the head of the road before her mother is finished with it, and once to see her half-brother and learn whether the hostage is soft.
people.secret: She skims a tenth of every toll her mother's band takes into a jar buried behind the cup tent, to buy riders who will follow her and not Đồ Xích Linh.

people.role: Captain of Dạ Quang's caravan escorts since 1121
people.appearance: A weathered, tidy rider from the camel-bell town who keeps the escort's ledgers in a hand better than his master's.
people.backstory: A camel-bell trader's son of Đà Linh Trấn, he rode in the raids as a young man and was made escort captain when the raiders were set to guarding the caravans they had robbed (A123). To everyone's surprise he is good at it, and likes being paid. He posts his legs on the board at the Đà Linh well so that small traders can join his train for a share of the fee, and he does not know who else reads it. Trấn Sa Đường's watcher Nhiếp Cô Đăng (nhiep_co_dang) follows every escort he rides. He is the one Dạ Quang man the merchants of Hồi Lan Thành trust.
people.wants: A road where any small trader can join his train without fear, and enough saved to retire to Đà Linh Trấn with a ledger-house of his own.
people.secret: He has begun posting false legs on the Đà Linh board, routes his escort never rides, to see whether wrapped riders come for them; the day they do, he will know whose band it is, and Đồ Xích Linh reads that board.

people.backstory: A Hồi Lan Thành merchant's daughter taken in a raid in 1080 who chose to stay, married Hạng Dạ Bôi (hang_da_boi), and kept Dạ Quang's books for forty years.
